harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL9, MariaDB 10.5 + galera 26.4) with wsrep replication over the private cluster network. Verified multi-master write visibility across all members, verified continued availability and automatic resync when a member is taken down and brought back, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time node restart protocol on all three nodes with proof of changed boot identity and full cluster/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera, rsync on node1/node2/node3 (RHEL9 AppStream repos)
Appended CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on node2 and node3 (node1 already had them)
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4444/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp on all 3 nodes (SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered these ports)

Edited /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node: wsrep_on=1, wsrep_cluster_name=galera_cluster, wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://10.100.154.10,10.100.154.11,10.100.154.12, per-node wsrep_node_name/wsrep_node_address, wsrep_sst_method=rsync
Bootstrapped the cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb normally on node2 and node3 to join via SST/IST
Enabled mariadb.service on all 3 nodes for boot persistence
Set root password and created replicated galera_app user (via mysql.global_priv, InnoDB, replicates through Galera) using secret_env-passed credentials
Created galeratest.t table and demonstrated cross-node write visibility (insert on node1/node2/node3, select from all)

Stopped mariadb on node3 to simulate a member outage, confirmed cluster stayed Primary at size 2 and accepted writes on node1/node2, restarted mariadb on node3 and confirmed automatic IST resync (state Synced, cluster size 3) with outage-period rows present

Executed mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on all nodes, rebooted node1/node2/node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified cluster size 3 / Primary / Synced / consistent row count after each individual restart before proceeding to the next node

evidence.requirement: Three-node Galera cluster formed, writes through any member visible on others
evidence.summary: Cluster bootstrapped on node1, node2 and node3 joined and reached wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced with cluster_size=3; inserts made from node1, node2, and node3 each showed up on all other nodes' SELECT results.

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: mariadb stopped on node3; cluster remained wsrep_cluster_status=Primary at size 2 on node1, and both node1 and node2 accepted and cross-replicated new writes while node3 was down.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member resynchronizes automatically when it returns
evidence.summary: mariadb restarted on node3 with no manual resync steps; it automatically rejoined via IST, reached wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced with cluster_size=3, and its galeratest.t table contained the rows written on node1/node2 during its outage.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 31949c21.../cluster healthy(size3,Synced,count5) captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then boot_id changed to e9165b83...; post-restart cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, count=5 confirmed.

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 55595e92.../cluster healthy captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to bbacda14... after reconnect; post-restart cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, count=5 confirmed.

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4999270d.../cluster healthy captured (this was after node3's earlier outage/resync test); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 0618d422... after reconnect; post-restart cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, count=5 confirmed. Restarts were performed strictly one node at a time, each verified fully synced before proceeding to the next.
